newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says no deaths in Timor clash - agency.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says no deaths in Timor clash - agency.

text.p: The Indonesian military in East Timor has denied reports that six people were killed during brawls between young Catholics and members of a military-backed group early this month, Antara news agency reported on Sunday.

"It is totally untrue the reports saying that six people have been killed in the clash... It is not true, nobody has died," East Timor military commander Colonel Mahidin Simbolon was quoted by the official agency as saying on Saturday.
Simbolon, who spoke in Dili, capital of the former Portuguese territory, also denied reports that a number of Catholic priests had been beaten during the brawls.

Church sources have said fights broke out after members of the military-backed Gada Paksi youth organisation attacked 10 Catholic youths, a priest and his driver on February 7 in Viqueque, about 100 km (60 miles) east of Dili.

One source said the Gada Paksi members beat the priest and the youths after accusing them of trying to hold an illegal meeting. Fights between the two groups continued until February 9, the source said.
Some sources said they heard rumours that at least six people died in the fights.
Simbolon said the brawls were purely criminal and that the authorities had confiscated daggers, stones and other objects from the suspects.

East Timor deputy chief Lieutenant-Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters on Saturday that the police were searching for more suspects and that they were still questioning the 109 people so far arrested after the fights.
"We still question the 109 people. They could be charged with property destruction or carrying (a) sharp weapon, which is illegal here. We continue searching for more suspects," he said.
Military and police officials have declined to say whether Gada Paksi members were among those still being held, but church sources have said no members of the group had been arrested.

The London-based rights group Amnesty International, in a statement on Saturday, urged Indonesian authorities to ensure that none of the detainees was tortured or ill-treated and that they were given immediate access to lawyers, family members or medical treatment when necessary.

Gada Paksi, the Youth Guard of Integration Upholders, was set up in 1995 and its members receive military-style training in Java. East Timorese residents have accused members of the group of intimidating people who oppose the territory's integration with Indonesia.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later, a move not recognised by the United Nations.
